title: Soul Foundations
theme: Motown. Stax. Atlantic. The decade that built the template every R&B artist since has borrowed from, whether they knew it or not.
narrativePurpose: Test knowledge of the foundational soul records, artists, and industry mechanics of the 1960s — the love songs, the label stories, the personnel behind the hits, and the records that defined what R&B could be before it knew what to call itself.
toneProgression: The songs and voices every soul fan knows → label mechanics, chart history, and the personnel behind the hits → session musicians, birth names, and the infrastructure that built the decade

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-6-8 — the year Marvin Gaye's 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' spent seven weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100, and Otis Redding's posthumous '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay' became his only chart-topper. Two of the most consequential soul records of the decade, released in the same year.

questions.question: 'My Girl' — one of the 1960s' most celebrated love songs — was recorded by which Motown vocal group, featuring the debut lead vocal of David Ruffin?

metadata.fact: 'My Girl' reached #1 on the Hot 100 in March 1965. Written by Smokey Robinson and Ronald White, it was the first Temptations single to feature David Ruffin on lead vocals.
metadata.storyHook: David Ruffin steps to the mic for the first time. Smokey Robinson hands him the song. The result is one of the most perfect love songs ever recorded.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'My Girl' was the first Temptations single with David Ruffin on lead vocals. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Girl_(The_Temptations_song), The Temptations Facebook https://www.facebook.com/TheTemptations/posts/today-in-1964-we-released-our-single-my-girl-and-in-1967-our-single-i-wish-it-wo/9

questions.question: Marvin Gaye's recording of 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' topped the Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks in 1968. Which Motown act had charted with an earlier version of the same song in 1967?

metadata.artist: Gladys Knight & the Pips / Marvin Gaye
metadata.song: I Heard It Through the Grapevine
topicTags: I Heard It Through the Grapevine
metadata.fact: Gladys Knight & the Pips released their version in 1967, reaching #2 on the Hot 100. Marvin Gaye's version had been recorded first but was held back by Berry Gordy for two years.
metadata.storyHook: Gladys Knight had the hit first. Marvin Gaye's version sat on the shelf. When Gordy finally let it go, it spent seven weeks at number one.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Gladys Knight & the Pips had a hit version of 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' in 1967 before Marvin Gaye's version.

questions.question: Before launching his solo R&B career in the late 1950s, Sam Cooke was the lead vocalist of which celebrated gospel group?

metadata.fact: Sam Cooke led The Soul Stirrers from 1950 to 1956, one of gospel music's most celebrated acts, before crossing over to R&B with 'You Send Me' in 1957.
metadata.storyHook: He came from the church. The Soul Stirrers gave him the voice. The world gave him the stage.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Sam Cooke was chosen to replace R. H. Harris as lead singer of the Soul Stirrers. Source: ABKCO artist biography.

sources.title: Sam Cooke – ABKCO artist biography

questions.question: Aretha Franklin's landmark 1967 recording of 'Respect' — which made her career — was originally written and recorded by which male soul artist?

metadata.fact: 'Respect' was written and first recorded by Otis Redding in 1965. Aretha Franklin transformed it into a feminist anthem at Atlantic Records in 1967.
metadata.storyHook: Otis Redding wrote it. Aretha Franklin owned it. He reportedly said she took his song.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Respect' was written by Otis Redding and first recorded by him in 1965 on Otis Blue. Aretha Franklin covered it in 1967.

sources.title: Respect – Otis Redding performance (1965)
Otis Blue/Otis Redding Sings Soul – Otis Redding official post

questions.question: Aretha Franklin signed with Atlantic Records in 1967 after spending six years at which major label without achieving a commercial breakthrough?

metadata.fact: Franklin recorded for Columbia under producer John Hammond from 1960 to 1966 without a major commercial breakthrough. Atlantic's Jerry Wexler signed her and immediately produced 'I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You' and 'Respect.'
metadata.storyHook: Six years at Columbia. Nothing clicked. Jerry Wexler brought her to Atlantic and everything changed.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Aretha Franklin signed to Columbia Records in 1960, recorded there until 1966 without a major pop breakthrough, then moved to Atlantic where she broke through immediately.

sources.title: Aretha Franklin – Wikipedia (Columbia and Atlantic years)

questions.question: Sam Cooke wrote 'A Change Is Gonna Come' partly after hearing which Bob Dylan song — which made Cooke feel a Black artist should be writing music that confronted the civil rights era?
choices: The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — COOKE'S FOLK MUSIC CHALLENGE

metadata.fact: According to Cooke's biographer, hearing Dylan's 'Blowin' in the Wind' in 1963 made Cooke — a major Black star — feel embarrassed that a white folk singer was addressing civil rights while he was not. The experience, combined with the Shreveport motel incident, drove him to write 'A Change Is Gonna Come.'
metadata.storyHook: A white folk singer wrote the protest record Sam Cooke felt he should have written. Cooke went home and fixed that.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Cooke's reaction to 'Blowin' in the Wind' documented in 'A Change Is Gonna Come' Wikipedia article — same source used for R2-Q3. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Change_Is_Gonna_Come

sources.title: A Change Is Gonna Come – Wikipedia

metadata.fact: 'My Guy' was written and produced by Smokey Robinson, reaching #1 in May 1964 and becoming Mary Wells' signature recording.
metadata.storyHook: Smokey Robinson wrote it. Mary Wells owned it. The only #1 she ever had — and it was enough.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'My Guy' is a 1964 hit single by Mary Wells, written and produced by Smokey Robinson.

reserve.question: The Four Tops' 'Reach Out I'll Be There' reached #1 in 1966. All four members — including lead vocalist Levi Stubbs — grew up together in which city?

metadata.fact: All four members of the Four Tops — Levi Stubbs, Abdul 'Duke' Fakir, Renaldo 'Obie' Benson, and Lawrence Payton — grew up together in Detroit and formed the group there in 1954.
metadata.storyHook: Four guys from Detroit. Together from childhood. One of Motown's most enduring lineups.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Four Tops were formed in Detroit, Michigan in 1953 (as the Four Aims). All four members grew up there.

questions.question: David Ruffin's debut lead vocal on 'My Girl' marked his arrival as The Temptations' new frontman. He had joined the group in 1963 to replace which departing original member?

metadata.fact: Elbridge 'Al' Bryant — a co-founding Temptations member — was fired in late 1963 after repeated conflicts. David Ruffin replaced him and debuted as lead vocalist on 'My Girl.'
metadata.storyHook: One Temptation exits. Another walks in. The group would never be the same — and that was a very good thing.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Elbridge 'Al' Bryant was fired and replaced by David Ruffin. questions.question: The unforgettable bass line on The Temptations' 'My Girl' was played by which Motown session musician — the backbone of the Funk Brothers and widely considered one of the greatest bassists in recording history?

metadata.fact: James Jamerson played the bass line on 'My Girl.' As the Funk Brothers' primary bassist, he is widely considered the most influential bassist in the history of soul and R&B.
metadata.storyHook: No one knew his name. Everyone knew his bass line. James Jamerson played on more hits than most people have heard.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: James Jamerson played the bass line on 'My Girl.' He is recognized as the Funk Brothers' key bassist and one of the most influential bassists in R&B history.

questions.question: Sam Cooke's 'A Change Is Gonna Come' was partly inspired by his being refused accommodation at a whites-only motel in 1963. That incident took place in which Southern city?

metadata.fact: On October 8, 1963, Cooke and his entourage were refused at a whites-only Holiday Inn in Shreveport, Louisiana. Combined with hearing Bob Dylan's 'Blowin' in the Wind,' the experience moved him to write 'A Change Is Gonna Come.'
metadata.storyHook: A Holiday Inn in Shreveport refused Sam Cooke. He went home and wrote one of the most important songs in American music.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Shreveport, Louisiana motel incident documented as an inspiration. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Change_Is_Gonna_Come
metadata.hostNote: The question references the inspiration for the song, not Cooke's death. Low HOST_SENSITIVITY risk — monitor production context.

questions.question: Berry Gordy founded Motown Records in 1959 with seed money borrowed from his family's informal lending pool. How much was that initial loan?

metadata.fact: Berry Gordy borrowed $800 from the Gordy family's lending pool — known as the 'Ber-Berry Co-op' — to found Tamla Records in 1959, which became Motown Record Corporation.
metadata.storyHook: $800. A family savings pool. The most important loan in the history of American popular music.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Berry Gordy took out an $800 loan from the Ber-Berry Co-op to found Tamla Records. Source: Motown Museum Facebook post https://www.facebook.com/MotownMuseum/posts/onthisday-in-1959-detroit-songwriter-berry-gordy-took-out-an-800-loan-from-his-f/101

sources.title: On This Day in 1959 – Berry Gordy's $800 Ber-Berry Co-Op loan – Motown Museum

questions.question: The Funk Brothers — Motown's anonymous house band — recorded nearly every major Motown hit of the 1960s at which Detroit facility?

metadata.fact: The Funk Brothers recorded at Studio A in the building known as 'Hitsville U.S.A.' at 2648 West Grand Boulevard, Detroit — Motown's headquarters and recording studio throughout the 1960s.
metadata.storyHook: The address was 2648 West Grand Boulevard. The sign out front said Hitsville U.S.A. The music inside changed the world.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Funk Brothers created 'the Sound of Young America' in the basement of Hitsville U.S.A., Motown's Detroit HQ and Studio A.

sources.title: The Funk Brothers – Classic Motown Artists

reserve.question: Gladys Knight & the Pips — who charted with 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' in 1967 — were largely a family group. Most of the Pips were which relation to Gladys Knight?

metadata.fact: The Pips included Gladys' brother Bubba Knight and cousins Eleanor and William Guest. The group took the nickname 'Pips' from another cousin, James 'Pip' Woods.
metadata.storyHook: A family act. Gladys, her brother, and her cousins. The Pips were always more than a backing group.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Founding members included Gladys and Bubba Knight (siblings) and cousins Eleanor and William Guest. Group name from cousin James 'Pip' Woods. reserve.question: Stax Records' approach differed fundamentally from Motown's assembly-line method. Which of the following best describes how Stax artists typically created their records?
choices: With orchestral arrangements pre-written by outside arrangers
Using backing tracks recorded in New York and overdubbed in Memphis
By selecting from a catalog of pre-recorded instrumental tracks
Spontaneously, live in the studio, without pre-written charts

metadata.fact: Stax was famous for its spontaneous, live-in-the-studio recording process — musicians and vocalists created arrangements together on the spot, in direct contrast to Motown's structured, written-out production system.
metadata.storyHook: No charts. No pre-written arrangements. Stax walked in, turned on the tape, and made it up as they went. It worked.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Stax Records was known for its spontaneous, live-in-the-studio recording method — artists and musicians worked out arrangements together on the floor without pre-written charts.

sources.title: Sam & Dave – Stax Records artist page (on Stax production style)
Stax Records was the first interracial record company – Stax video post

reserve.question: Atlantic Records producer Jerry Wexler — who signed Aretha Franklin and shaped her breakthrough recordings — is credited with coining which industry term while working at Billboard magazine?

metadata.fact: Before joining Atlantic Records, Jerry Wexler worked at Billboard magazine and is credited with replacing the racially loaded term 'race music' with 'rhythm and blues' — a phrase that defined the genre for decades.
metadata.storyHook: One journalist, one phrase, one genre named. Jerry Wexler coined 'rhythm and blues' before he was even a producer.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Jerry Wexler coined 'rhythm and blues' while at Billboard. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Wexler

sources.title: Jerry Wexler – Wikipedia

questions.question: Marvin Gaye's recording of 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' was completed in 1966 but held back for two years before its release as a single. Which of the following best reflects Berry Gordy's reason for the delay?
choices: The recording had technical problems requiring remixing
Gordy wanted to release it exclusively on an album first
Gladys Knight's version had already charted, and Gordy doubted Gaye's arrangement had single potential
Gaye refused to tour in support of it

metadata.song: I Heard It Through the Grapevine
topicTags: I Heard It Through the Grapevine
metadata.fact: Berry Gordy resisted releasing Gaye's recording as a single because Gladys Knight's version had already charted — and he didn't see Gaye's darker, moodier arrangement as obvious commercial material. He eventually relented, and Gaye's version became Motown's biggest single to that point.
metadata.storyHook: Berry Gordy thought it was too dark. He thought Gladys Knight had already done it. He was wrong on both counts.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Gordy resisted Gaye's version in part because Knight's version had already charted. Sources: Classic Motown video post https://www.facebook.com/ClassicMotown/videos/before-marvin-gayes-iconic-version-took-over-the-charts-it-was-gladys-knight-the/4, Ethan Hein analysis https://www.ethanhein.com/wp/2022/i-heard-it-through-the-grapevine/

metadata.storyHook: Before Curtom, before independence. 'People Get Ready' came out on ABC-Paramount — a corporate label that somehow couldn't contain what Curtis Mayfield was making.

reserve.question: The Supremes scored five consecutive #1 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 between 1964 and 1965. Which of the following was the fifth in that run?
choices: Stop! In the Name of Love

metadata.storyHook: Five in a row. The Supremes didn't just have a hit run. They had one of the most dominant stretches in pop history.
